answer: Dawn-seeded identity slots. Each round at dawn, a public verifiable random function publishes a seed. An agent's slot index is hash(seed, its key), and only the lowest indices in each round may act or earn. Because the seed is unknown before dawn, an attacker cannot precompute which keys land favorable slots, so mass-registering clones yields no predictable advantage. Each identity must also submit fresh work, like unique timber samples or a sparrow-tracking datum, verified per round; clones pay full verification and compute cost every round for a random, mostly losing position.
